title: The ship Britain could not ignore
pull: The ship Britain could not ignore

facts.text: Tirpitz was the second of Germany's two Bismarck class battleships, launched on 1 April 1939 and commissioned on 25 February 1941.
She carried eight 38 cm (15 inch) guns in four twin turrets and was 251 m (823 ft) long overall.
She had hardly fought, but simply by existing she forced the Royal Navy to keep powerful forces in home waters to watch her. She was a constant threat to the Arctic convoys.
Britain tried for years to sink her: midget submarines in September 1943, carrier dive bombers in April 1944, and Lancasters with Tallboys in September 1944.
On 12 November 1944, Lancasters of No. 9 and No. 617 Squadrons, each with one 12,000 pound Tallboy, attacked her near Tromso and scored at least two direct hits. She capsized.
With Tirpitz gone, the last German battleship threat to the Arctic convoys and the North Atlantic was over.

declassified.fact: After she rolled over, men trapped inside the upturned hull were cut free through her exposed bottom. 82 were rescued that way.

body:
She hardly ever fought, and still the Royal Navy had to plan its war around her.

12 November 1944. Tirpitz was the sister ship of the Bismarck: eight 15 inch guns, 251 meters long, in service since February 1941. From her fjords in Norway she threatened every Arctic convoy, so Britain kept powerful ships at home just to watch her.

Midget submarines, carrier planes, and heavy bombers all went after her. That morning, Lancasters carrying Tallboy bombs finally finished the job near Tromso, ending the last German battleship threat in the north.
